correctness.rationale: The coexistence equilibrium has Hurwitz Jacobian J=[[-gamma,-an],[C,0]] with det D>0. A frequency-independent stable causal convolution bound and quadratic remainder yield a unique nearby positive periodic branch for bounded forcing and O(epsilon²) errors uniformly in frequency. Solving (i omega I-J)H=u e1 gives H_N=uiomega/(D-omega²+i gamma omega), H_P=uC/(D-omega²+i gamma omega), hence exact leading amplitudes RN=u omega/sqrt(Q), RP=uC/sqrt(Q) and phase lag -pi/2. The minimum forcing for both separate minima is S(omega)=sqrt(Q)/u max(dN/omega,dP/C). For omega below omega_cross=C dN/dP, prey branch decreases to omega_N=sqrt(D) then increases; above the crossover, predator branch decreases to omega_P=sqrt(max(D-gamma²/2,0)) then increases, with 0≤omega_P<omega_N. The clamp trichotomy is the unique global minimizer; prey gain vanishes at both omega endpoints, keeping near-optimal frequencies compact and transferring the leading minimax to nonlinear response. The proof explicitly does not infer tipping or simultaneous-in-time crossing; near-resonance numerical checks only corroborate the algebra.
